 J U D G M E N T
This petition under Section 166 M.V.Act is filed seeking compensation of .5,00,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 13072019 about 3.00 a.m., the Petitioner was travelling in a Cab bearing No.KA05AA4963 from CISCO company towards Mallathahalli and when the car reached near Jayanagar 9th Block, Marenahalli 100 feet ring road, 28th Main Road junction, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA18MH0279 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle)
drove the same in high speed and in rash and negligent manner, dashed against the Cab to the right side front.
Due to which the driver of Petitioner's car lost control and dashed against the electric pole and the Petitioner sustained severe injuries and driver has also sustained injuries.

He was immediately taken to Malathi Manipal hospital, Jayanagar, after first aid, he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Old Airport Road, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient as he has sustained severe traumatic brain injury, diffuse axona injury and in unconscious state.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to his native place hospital i.e., EMS memorial cooperative hospital and Research center Ltd., Panabi Malapuram, Kerala and from the date of accident till today he is under treatment, but no improvement in his condition and he is totally depending on others and not in conscious and bedridden.

Due to the accidental injuries he is suffering from permanent disability Vijesh.A vs Kishore Kumar Hegade on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4739223/
2 and unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that parents of the Petitioner have spent huge amount for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.
At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 29 years, he was working permanently at ARICENT Technologies and he was drawing salary of .11,00,000/ p.a.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.

As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1 Insured and Respondent No.2Insurer of offending car.
3. In response to the petition notice, all the Respondents have appeared before the court through their counsel and Respondent No.1, 2 and 4 have filed their written statement.
The Respondent No.3 has not filed the written statement.
4. The Respondent No.1RC owner of offending car has denied the entire petition averments.

He has admitted that Respondent No.1 is the RC owner of offending vehicle and the same was insured with Respondent No.2 and policy was valid as on the date of accident and the driver was holding valid DL.

It is contended that the accident was not due to negligence of driver of offending vehicle,
but it was due to the negligence of driver of Car bearing No.KA05AG4963.

He has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed is arbitrary and speculative and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. The Respondent No.2insurance company has disputes the issuance of policy in respect of offending vehicle.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It has also contended that the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle in causing the accident.
On the other hand, the accident has occurred due to negligence of driver of Car bearing No.KA05AA4963 and he had also contributed more negligence for the accident.
Further it has contended that the compensation claimed by Petitioner is highly excessive and arbitrary.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner,
and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
On these grounds, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. The Respondent No.4insurer of Etios Car bearing No.KA052AG4963 has contended that the 3rd Respondent is not the RC owner of the Car bearing No.KA052AG4963 and policy was issued in favour of one Nagendra T.K.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It has also contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the negligence of the driver of Car bearing No.KA05AG4963.
On the other hand, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Jeep bearing No.KA18MH0279.
Further it has contended that the compensation claimed by Petitioner is highly excessive and arbitrary.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
On these grounds, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 13072019 about 3.00 a.m. when he was traveling in ETIOS car bearing No.KA05AG4963 towards Mallathahalli at Jayanagar 9th Block, Marenahalli 100 feet Ring road, 28th Main Road junction, a Jeep car bearing No.KA18MH279 came in a high speed and rash and negligently dashed against the car in which the Petitioner was sitting, due to which the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If how much and from whom?
3. What order?

8. In order to prove the claim, the father of Petitioner is examined as PW.1, Manager of ARICENT is examined as PW2, Medical record assistant officer is examined as PW3, Senior team member,
MRD at Manipal hospital is examined as PW4, Senior Resident doctor at CMC hospital, Vellore is examined as PW5, Medical Record Librarian, EMS Memorial Cooperative hospitals, Kerals is examined as PW6, Secretary, Administration, Niramaya hospital, Kerala is examined as PW7 and Managing Director of Mother Rehab Multispeciality hospital, Kerala is examined as PW8 and Manager HR, Global Edge Solutions Ltd., Bengaluru is examined a PW9 and in all 60 documents are got marked as per Ex.P.1 to P.60.

11. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S 12.
ISSUE NO.1:
In order to prove his claim, Petitioner's father is examined as PW.1 since the Petitioner was unable to appear before the court and he was not capable of giving evidence as he is in vegetative state.

PW1 relied on the police and medical records and he has deposed that on 13 072019 about 3.00 a.m., his son i.e., Petitioner was travelling in a Cab bearing No.KA05AA 4963 from CISCO company towards Mallathahalli and when the car reached near Jayanagar 9th Block, Marenahalli 100 feet ring road, 28th Main Road junction, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver Vijesh.A vs Kishore Kumar Hegade on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4739223/
4 of Car bearing Reg.No.KA18MH0279 drove the same in high speed and in rash and negligent manner, dashed against the Cab to the right side front.
Due to which the driver of Petitioner's car lost control and dashed against the electric pole and the Petitioner sustained severe injuries and driver has also sustained injuries.
It is stated that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

13. In support of his claim, PW1 has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, complaint at Ex.P.2, spot sketch at Ex.P.3, spot mahazar at Ex.P.4, IMV report at Ex.P.5, Wound certificates at Ex.P.6, notice and reply at Ex.P.7 & 8 and charge sheet at Ex.P.9.
As per wound certificate he has sustained grievous injuries to his head and other injuries all over the body.
14. So far as the negligence is concerned insurance company has contended that it was also the negligence of driver of the car in which the Petitioner was proceeding.
On the application filed by the Respondent No.2 insurance company, the RC owner and the insurer of the car bearing No.KA05 AG4963 are also impleaded as 3rd and 4th Respondent in this petition.
The insurer of the offending Jeep car bearing No.KA18MH0279 has contended that it was the sole negligence of the driver of the Petitioner's car.

Making reliance on the sketch produced at Ex.P.3, 2nd respondent  insurance company has argued that the accident has taken place in the middle of the junction and the driver of the car in which the Petitioner was proceeding, was driving it in high speed and lost control and dashed to the road side pole.
When the vehicle dashed the pole, Petitioner head got hit to the front seat and he sustained head injury only due to the negligence of driver of the Petitioner's car alone.
15. The second Respondent insurance company has also relied on the IMV report and the wound certificate of the Petitioner.
It is argued that according to the IMV report and the sketch, front portion of the petitioner's car bearing No.KA05AG4963 is damaged due to the road side pole.

If at all the insured vehicle had dashed the said car, the right side of the door would have damaged and the Petitioner as well as the driver of the said car would also have sustained severe injuries.
No damages on the right side of the car and no other injuries to the Petitioner and the driver, clearly indicates that the offending car has not dashed the Petitioner's car.

It is alleged that the driver of the Petitioner's car was driving it in a high speed, he lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the roadside pole and due to that only the Petitioner sustained injuries only on the head.
16. In order to prove this contention, insurance company examined it's official as RW3.
He has deposed according to the above contention and said that it was the negligence of the driver of the Petitioner's car and there was no negligence on the part of the insured car.
17. After impleading the driver cum owner of car bearing No.KA05AG4963, 4th Respondent examined him as RW2 and he deposed that it was not his negligence in causing the accident.
During cross examination he admits that the place of accident is a junction and due to the accident he lost control and dashed to the road side pole.
Second Respondent insurance company stressed on the point that on the date of accident the driver had trip at 10:00 PM and returned at 11:00 PM.
He slept at Cisco office and after completion of the work of the Petitioner, he woke up and went to drop him.
He left the office at 2:15 AM.

It is argued that it was in the middle of the night almost early in Vijesh.A vs Kishore Kumar Hegade on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4739223/
5 the morning and the driver had less sleep, it was his negligence in causing the accident as he was in high speed.

It is alleged that being a driver of the taxi he is aware of the consequences and taking advantage of the inmates of the insured car had left the place, he filed false complaint against the driver of insured vehicle.
It is argued that as it was the early morning the driver was drowsy he was driving the car with high speed.
When he entered the junction, after seeing the other car, while controlling the vehicle, he dashed the road side pole due to which the Petitioner sustained injuries.

It is the contention of the second Respondent insurance company that if at all the offending car had dashed the Petitioner's car either the Petitioner or the driver would have sustained fractures or any severe injuries, but except the head injury to the Petitioner absolutely there are no injuries and hence it is contended that the insured car or the alleged offending car never hit the car of the Petitioner.
18.
Both parties have filed written arguments and it is the contention of the Petitioner that the driver of the offending car was alone responsible for the accident.
Since the offending car had hit the car of the Petitioner, the driver lost control and dashed to the road side pole.

It is argued that if at all it was not the negligence of the offending car, why the driver and inmates left the spot immediately after the accident and why they have not filed any complaint with the police; Why the driver of the offending car is facing trial instead of challenging the FIR and chargesheet filed against him; Neither the RC owner nor the driver of the offending car have appeared before the court and gave any evidence.
The RC owner has replied to the notice issued by the police under Section 133 MV Act.
But he or the driver of the offending car have not given any statement to the police stating that it was not their negligence.
Police have investigated the matter in detail and filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending car.
Hence it is argued that it is only the negligence of driver of the offending car.

19. On perusal of entire materials on record it is to be noted that the accident took place about 2:00 A.M. in the morning and except inmates of these 2 vehicles there are no other eyewitnesses.
Complainant is none other than the driver of the car in which the Petitioner was proceeding and he alleged that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending car.
Absolutely there was no hindrance to the driver of the offending car, inmates of the car or the RC owner of the offending car to lodge complaint before the police or to give any statement.
It is to be noted that the FIR and the chargesheet filed by the investigating officer are not challenged however the accused is facing trial.
Accused has not stepped into the witness box though she is contesting the criminal case.
The second Respondent insurance company relied on the investigation report conducted by the insurance company, but no such report has been produced.
The RC owner of the offending car has not challenged or contested the petition.
Absolutely there are no materials or documents to prove the negligence of Respondent No.3 who is the driver of the car in which the Petitioner was proceeding.
20. So for as the damages to the vehicles are concerned, front right door of the Petitioner's car is damaged and so also the rear tail lamp assembly and rare right side bumper are also damaged.
The entire front portion of the offending car is damaged and there is no explanation for this by the second Respondent insurance company.

When it is alleged that since it was 2.00 a.m., driver of petitioner's car was drowsy having less sleep, same analogy can be applied to the driver of the offending car as she was not the professional driver.

All the materials clearly goes to show that the Vijesh.A vs Kishore Kumar Hegade on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4739223/
6 offending car was in high speed and dashed the car in which the Petitioner was proceeding.
Absolutely there are no materials to overcome the chargesheet findings.

All the documents produced by the Petitioner corroborate with his evidence and it is proved that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident only due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending car.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE NO.2:
The PW1 father of Petitioner states that Petitioner was aged about 29 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous traumatic brain injuries and was in unconscious state.

Immediately he was taken to Malathi Manipal hospital, after taking first aid,
he has taken treatment as an inpatient in Manipal hospital, Old Airport Road, Bengaluru and underwent several surgeries and still under treatment, but he was not recovered till today.
PW1 has stated that at the time of accident, his son was working as a Specialist Operations at ARICENT Technologies and he was drawing salary of .93,640/ p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he become unconscious till today and as such, he is unable to do the said work and suffered loss of income and he need future treatment and rehabilitation.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of future income.

The Petitioner has examined the medical record officers and employer of Petitioner as PW2 to 9.
22.
Disability:

Petitioner has stated that he has suffered grievous and severe traumatic brain injury in this accident and immediately after the accident he lost his consciousness and was shifted to emergency at Malathi Manipal Hospital Jayanagar.
Petitioner has relied on the wound certificate and discharge summaries of various hospitals in order to prove his disability.

According to wound certificate at Ex.P.6 he had sustained laceration on the scalp at right, CT brain showed diffuse Axonal injury with bleed in cerebellum, b/c temporal region, pons, midbrain hypothalamus, b/c thalamus, b/c frontal specs and conclusions, right sulcal SAH and corpus colossal bleed.

Medical records and case sheets of Malathi Manipal Hospital, Christian Medical College Vellore, EMS hospital, Kerala, Niramaya Ayurgreen hospital Kerala, Mother Rehab Multi Specialty Residential Physiotherapy Hospital, Kerala and Global Edge Solutions Limited are produced in order to show the present health condition of the Petitioner and what was the severity of injury sustained by him.

Counsel for Petitioner has argued that Petitioner was inpatient for more than 600 days and till today he is under treatment and the Petitioner is in a vegetative stage and needs to be feed through food pipe for every 2  hours.

It is argued that it is 100% disability and they relied on disability certificate issued by the Department Of Empowerment Of Persons With Disabilities Ministry Of Social Justice And Empowerment Government Of India.

According to this it is the case of locomotor disability diagnosed with traumatic brain injury, diffuse axonal injury quadriplegia bowel and bladder involvement.
The 100% disability is a permanent disability in relation to his brain and whole body.
27. The 2nd and 4th Respondent insurance companies have disputed this medical certificate contending that it was not authenticated and it cannot be trusted.
It is alleged that neither the expert doctor nor the doctor of treated hospitals have examined him in order to explain the medical condition of the Petitioner.
Petitioner was not produced before any neurosurgeon either here or in Kerala to examine him for the assessment of disability.
He said to have taken to Medical Board and obtained disability certificate.
The certificate produced is downloaded from the website.

there are no details who have examined the Petitioner; when he was taken to the medical board; or the author or the team of doctors who have assessed the disability have appeared before the court to give evidence; neither the medical certificate nor the issuing authority have subjected to cross examination.
It is argued that the disability certificate cannot be accepted for all these reasons.
28. Counsel for second Respondent vehemently argued that there are few reasons that the permanent disability of the Petitioner is doubtful.
Vijesh.A vs Kishore Kumar Hegade on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4739223/
8  The Petitioner is never brought before the court.
The Petitioner was never taken to the medical expert for assessment of disability who can come and give evidence before the court.
Though he was treated in several hospitals none of the treated doctors are examined in order to explain the treatment given to him and the present physical condition of the Petitioner.
There are no proof when Petitioner was taken to medical board for assessment of disability.

When the Petitioner is treated by spending lakhs of rupees, what was the impediment to bring him before the court or to take him to any treated doctor or expert either here in Bengaluru or in Kerala for assessment of disability.
The more stressed argument is that why the Petitioner was not removed from the job when his physical disability is said to be 100%.
Why the employer continued him as employee till 4 years when the Petitioner is said that he is not capable of working or he has suffered 100% disability.
It is also argued that the Petitioner is given exit from the job after once the employer came and give evidence before this court.
Moreover he was not removed or terminated, he was just given exit from the company that too at the request of his parents.

29. Counsel for the second Respondent argued that when these doubts are not resolved and the non production of the Petitioner either before the court or before any expert for assessment of disability and obtaining certificate online by producing him somewhere else, create doubt with regard to permanent disability of the Petitioner.
If at all his condition was that critical, he would have brought before the court or taken to the expert doctor and get the disability assessed.
It is also said that when the investigator from the insurance company tried to visit the Petitioner they were avoided by giving one or other reasons.
Hence it is argued that the Petitioner is not suffering the permanent disability to the extent of 100% and his physical condition is unknown and cannot be believed.

30. It is true that when there is traumatic brain injury and Petitioner has taken treatment for more than 600 days, what was the impediment for the Petitioner to examine a doctor either treated or any expert in order to prove the physical or neurological disability.
However, by considering continuous medical records indicate that he has suffered traumatic brain injury and he is in vegetative state.
Petitioner was presented before the court through video conference at the stage of arguments.
It is said that he is in vegetative state and not capable of even to move.
It was shown to the court that he was lying on the bed and there were no motor power as it is showed that his hands were fallen when it is hold and dropped.

31. Even though no doctor is examined, his case sheets, discharge summaries and other medical records such as CT scan reports indicate that he has suffered traumatic brain injury and appears to be in vegetative state till last date of discharge from the date of accident.
It is not proved otherwise that Petitioner is either capable of speaking or moving.

The continuous medical records indicate that Vijesh.A vs Kishore Kumar Hegade on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4739223/
9
his condition is still the same even after continuous treatment and physiotherapy.
In all the discharge summaries there are clear explanation of health condition of the Petitioner and it appears that he is in vegetative state with 100% physical disability.

32. Petitioner's counsel has relied on Judgments in Civil Appeal No.735/2020 in the case of Kajal vs.
Jagadish Chand and others dated 05022020, Civil Appeal No.6492/2021 in Jithendran vs. New India Assurance Co.Ltd., and another dated 27102021 and in Civil Appeal No.1540/2022 in Sri.Benson George Vs. Reliance Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., and another dated 25022022 and argued that the physical condition of the Petitioner must be considered and reasonable compensation shall be awarded.

sentences.text: 33. The disability certificate produced at EX.P.48 indicate that his case is of locomotor disability and the diagnosis was traumatic brain injury diffuse Axonal injury quadriplegia bowel and bladder involvement.

The medical authority under the department of empowerment of persons with disabilities has assessed the disability to the extent of 100% by saying that it is in relation to his brain, whole body as per RPWD Act, 2016 notified by Govt. of India.
Even though the certificate is not subjected to cross examination, this cannot be neglected or rejected at the threshold.

Even if the disability certificate is kept aside, the continuous medical records, discharge summaries indicate that he is in vegetative state till date and this will definitely show that he is disabled to the extent of 100% physically.

By considering the entire medical records, disability certificate, photographs of the Petitioner, arguments of the counsel for the Petitioner and other factors, I hold that the Petitioner is disabled to the extent of 100% physically and functionally.
34. The PW1 has stated that his son was aged about 29 years, in support of his age he has produced his Aadhaar card at Ex.P.23, which shows his year of birth as 1990.
As per which as on date of accident his age is considered as 29 years.

Therefore, the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 17.

.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to which the driver of Petitioner's car lost control and dashed against the electric pole and the Petitioner sustained severe injuries and driver has also sustained injuries.

opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The insurer of the offending Jeep car bearing No.KA18MH0279 has contended that it was the sole negligence of the driver of the Petitioner's car.
It is alleged that being a driver of the taxi he is aware of the consequences and taking advantage of the inmates of the insured car had left the place, he filed false complaint against the driver of insured vehicle.
Absolutely there was no hindrance to the driver of the offending car, inmates of the car or the RC owner of the offending car to lodge complaint before the police or to give any statement.
Accused has not stepped into the witness box though she is contesting the criminal case.
The second Respondent insurance company relied on the investigation report conducted by the insurance company, but no such report has been produced.
The RC owner of the offending car has not challenged or contested the petition.
Absolutely there are no materials or documents to prove the negligence of Respondent No.3 who is the driver of the car in which the Petitioner was proceeding.
The entire front portion of the offending car is damaged and there is no explanation for this by the second Respondent insurance company.
When it is alleged that since it was 2.00 a.m., driver of petitioner's car was drowsy having less sleep, same analogy can be applied to the driver of the offending car as she was not the professional driver.
All the materials clearly goes to show that the Vijesh.A vs Kishore Kumar Hegade on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4739223/
6 offending car was in high speed and dashed the car in which the Petitioner was proceeding.

It is alleged that neither the expert doctor nor the doctor of treated hospitals have examined him in order to explain the medical condition of the Petitioner.
Petitioner was not produced before any neurosurgeon either here or in Kerala to examine him for the assessment of disability.
He said to have taken to Medical Board and obtained disability certificate.
there are no details who have examined the Petitioner; when he was taken to the medical board; or the author or the team of doctors who have assessed the disability have appeared before the court to give evidence; neither the medical certificate nor the issuing authority have subjected to cross examination.
It is not proved otherwise that Petitioner is either capable of speaking or moving.
his condition is still the same even after continuous treatment and physiotherapy.
In all the discharge summaries there are clear explanation of health condition of the Petitioner and it appears that he is in vegetative state with 100% physical disability.
The medical authority under the department of empowerment of persons with disabilities has assessed the disability to the extent of 100% by saying that it is in relation to his brain, whole body as per RPWD Act, 2016 notified by Govt. of India.
Even though the certificate is not subjected to cross examination, this cannot be neglected or rejected at the threshold.
Even if the disability certificate is kept aside, the continuous medical records, discharge summaries indicate that he is in vegetative state till date and this will definitely show that he is disabled to the extent of 100% physically.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Respondent No.1 being the insured of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.
However, Respondent No.2 insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner with interest @ 6% p.a.
There is no liability of Respondent No.3 and 4.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
64. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost only against the Respondent No.1 and 2.
Petition against Respondent No.3 and 4 stands dismissed.
15 Petitioner is awarded compensation of .3,27,72,407/ together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall liable to pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this Order.
Out of the compensation amount a sum of .50,00,000/ shall be kept in FD in the name of Petitioner in any nationalized bank of Petitioner's choice for a period of 5 years.
Remaining amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner's guaridan through E payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
